transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
The Trump administration announced its rolling back fuel economy standards for new vehicles.
Willa Rubin reports it's a step that weakens Biden-era climate policies.
The corporate average fuel economy, CAFE standards, have been around since the '70s.
These require American carmakers to make each year's new vehicles more fuel efficient on
average across their entire fleets.
But how much more efficient?
Under the Biden administration, fleets needed to get 2 percent more efficient every year.
That meant carmakers needed to make electric vehicles, balance out their gas guzzlers,
otherwise they were subject to a fine.
That fine went away last July as part of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.
Now a much smaller increase in fuel efficiency will be required every year.
Willa Rubin, NPR News.
A New York prosecutor has reopened an investigation into gang rape allegations at a Cornell University
fraternity in response to a lawsuit.
The complaint was filed by a woman who says she was sexually assaulted in 2024 by seven
students after being plied with alcohol and drugs, NPR's Brian Mann reports.
In her civil lawsuit filed this month, the woman identified as Jane Doe describes a brutal
assault.
She wasn't old enough to drink legally, but says she was pressured at a CHI-5 fraternity
party to use alcohol and drugs.
She describes them being gang raped, often while she was incapacitated over a period
of hours.
The lawsuit filing includes a screen capture of Snapchat messages between some of the men
where they appear to joke and invite others to take part.
This lawsuit also accuses Cornell University of failing to properly respond to the alleged
violence.
I should say we don't know exactly what actions Cornell took against these individuals.
The university said some were suspended or expelled.
NPR's Brian Mann reporting.
Texas Attorney General and Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton told a forum of the U.S.
Hispanic Business Council in Fort Worth that the country needs to secure its border before
allowing in more immigrants.
But Paxton acknowledged that the key U.S. business sectors need more immigrants to fill
open jobs, as Houston Public Media's Andrew Schneider reports.
Paxton says that the U.S. needs to pursue an "America First" immigration policy that
benefits the people who are already here.
But he says he's spoken with farmers, ranchers and homebuilders who all rely on immigrant
workers.
And that likely means that we have to let people in that can fulfill some of these jobs
that we don't have enough people for.
Our birth population isn't keeping up with demand.
Paxton's Democratic opponent, State Representative James Talarico, will address the U.S. Hispanic
Business Council on Wednesday.
Talarico has been a fierce critic of both Paxton and President Trump when it comes to
immigration and border security.
I'm Andrew Schneider in Houston.
U.S. stocks pulled further from their record highs today.
The S&P 500 fell three-quarters of a percent.
This is NPR News.
Democrats are flocking to South Carolina to campaign for midterm candidates, even though
Republicans dominate the state's politics.
The Palmetto State is the first in Democrats' next presidential nominating process, so potential
2028 hopefuls are eager to visit in the coming weeks; Democrats like California Congressman
Ro Khanna, Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear and Arizona Senator Mark Kelly will all be
stumping in South Carolina.
The smoke billowing off of a wildfire can travel hundreds or thousands of miles.
A new field of study is trying to understand how that smoke may be disturbing wild places
and creatures, like birds.
Here's NPR's Ari Daniel.
Having repeatedly experienced wildfire smoke herself, Olivia Sanderfoot, who's based at
Cornell University, has long wanted to know how birds handle it.
It's not just about what they're inhaling, which is inevitably bad for them.
It's also about how the cues that they use to navigate their world are upended when it
gets smoky outside.
Sanderfoot's teamed up with researchers in other disciplines to create a new field called
smoke ecology.
It relies in part on birders already on the ground, collecting bird activity data when
smoke happens to blow in.
A top priority is to determine where birds go when it's smoky and what can be done to
help them.
Ari Daniel, NPR News.
With Major League Baseball's regular season wrapped up, the average time for a nine inning
game has increased by nearly four minutes this season, reaching two hours and 42 minutes.
This change follows the introduction of robot umpires, which allow players to appeal umpire
decisions to a computer.
This is NPR News.

New York prosecutor reopens investigation into gang rape allegations at Cornell University fraternity
Texas Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton says border security must come before increased immigration
U.S. stocks pull further from record highs, S&P 500 falls three-quarters of one percent
Democrats campaign in South Carolina ahead of 2028 presidential nominating process
Researchers create new field of smoke ecology to study wildfire smoke effects on birds
